meta.title: Sign & Sky
meta.description: Farmers' weather signs, tested against recorded rainfall, and returned by voice in English and Amharic.

home.title: What did the sky tell you today?

results.title: Field results, Wolaita 2025
results.intro: 17 indicators recorded with farmers in Wolaita, South Ethiopia. Each prediction was compared with historical recorded weather and scored out of 10.
results.trustRule: Strong is a score of 8 or more, fair is 6 to 7.9, weak is below 6.
results.methodField: The 17 field scores were calculated by the Sign & Sky AI, which compared the farmers' prediction with historical recorded scientific weather data for Wolaita. They are stored as recorded and marked “field-ai-2025”.
results.methodNew: New tests use a published, repeatable method (sns-score-v1). A sign seen on day D predicts an outcome within W days. The tool takes daily rainfall for the W days after D, and for the same calendar window in each of the N earlier years (10 by default).
results.formulaH: H is 1 if the predicted outcome happened in the window, otherwise 0.
results.formulaP: P is where this year's window ranks among the earlier years (0 to 1), turned toward the prediction: wetter counts for rain signs, drier for dry signs.
results.datasets: Data: ERA5 reanalysis through the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API, and CHIRPS daily rainfall once its extractor is connected. Every test keeps the request, the daily values, the thresholds and the calculation.
results.thresholds: Rain happened: at least 10 mm in the window. Heavy rain: one day of 20 mm or more. Start of the rains: 3 days totalling 20 mm with at least 2 wet days. Normal: between the 25th and 75th percentile. Dry: under 5 mm or under half the usual amount. Drought: at or below the 20th percentile.

about.title: About Sign & Sky
about.lead: Farmers have read the sky, the trees and the animals for generations. Sign & Sky records those signs, tests each one against recorded weather, and gives the result back to farmers in their own language.
promises: Every sign stays credited to the community it came from. Farmers' names and villages are never published.
Every score shows how it was made: the data, the years compared and the calculation.
A weak score is said plainly. We never call a sign reliable when the data does not support it.
Amharic text is marked for review until a native speaker has checked it.
how: Listen: the farmer speaks or types a sign.
Understand: Sign & Sky recognises the sign and reads the place and season.
Test: the sign's score against recorded weather is looked up, or the sign is saved for testing.
Voice advice: the answer is spoken and written.
about.seasonsEthiopia: Ethiopia: Belg March–May, Kiremt / Meher June–September, Bega October–February.
about.seasonsIndia: India: pre-monsoon March–May, monsoon June–September, post-monsoon October–February.
about.placesText: Scores were recorded in Wolaita, South Ethiopia. Farmers in Telangana and Haryana, India can use the assistant too; their answers say where the sign was tested.
about.dataText: Recorded weather comes from ERA5 reanalysis and, when connected, CHIRPS satellite rainfall.
about.apiText: The published library, in both languages with every test result, is open at {url} for apps such as the offline Sign & Sky Android app.
about.teamText: Sign & Sky was created by a team that won the UN Hackathon on AI for Good with the idea of joining indigenous weather knowledge with satellite and reanalysis data.

footer.line: Sign & Sky — indigenous weather knowledge, tested and returned to farmers.
footer.note: Advice here supports, and does not replace, official forecasts and local extension officers.
